account:
Today the unusual thing is repeated talk of a 'bridge or port change' near the bakery, without any concrete proposal reaching me. I personally heard Townsfolk 01 and 11 repeat those words this morning. The neighbour has also heard vague repetitions near the bakery, but explicitly has no firsthand description, dates, or observations of changes along the quay. I tried to ask the baker directly, but the baker left before hearing my question. I do not know who originated this talk, whether any change is actually planned, or what it would be for. Repetition alone is not evidence of an organised project or wrongdoing.

Town business has also been frustratingly incomplete. At the scheduled mill inspection I found grain offered at the mill stall, but no miller or responsible manager to answer questions. I saw 68 hay bales listed at two emeralds each; I did not establish grain quality and have approved nothing. The secretary has been unable to identify the manager. At the council-letters appointment, neither of us had correspondence to address. The secretary said she would record that absence, seek a mill contact from the baker or freight organiser, and invite the actual bridge or port proposers to explain their plans tomorrow morning. I cannot yet say whether any of that follow-up has succeeded. My later dictated inspection letter was not heard, so I should not assume it was drafted.

I am currently finishing the confirmed afternoon tea at the neighbour's cottage. The neighbour has been hospitable and careful not to present rumours as facts. I heard the secretary shouting in the distance shortly before four, but could not understand the words and do not know what prompted it. My next commitments are office at 16:30 and the builder's great hall lighting inspection at 18:00, followed by home at 19:00. The lighting appointment is a known, scheduled inspection; I have no evidence connecting it to the bridge or port talk. My best course is to keep these commitments and obtain specific firsthand accounts rather than infer a hidden purpose from vague news.
